properties.text: The p256verify precompile MUST NOT revert under any circumstances except out-of-gas. For all inputs (including malformed, zero-length, or adversarial inputs), the precompile must return either 32-byte success (0x01) or empty bytes (failure), never triggering an EVM revert.

reachability.notes: Any EOA or smart contract can invoke the precompile at address 0x100 via CALL/STATICCALL with arbitrary calldata. Reachable through normal transaction submission.

properties.severity_justification: A revert in the precompile would cause consensus divergence between clients that handle the revert differently, potentially leading to a chain split across the entire network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing a specific input that causes revert in at least one client implementation.

properties.text: The p256verify precompile input validation MUST follow a strict sequential order: (1) check input length == 160 bytes, (2) check 0 < r < n, (3) check 0 < s < n, (4) check 0 <= qx < p, (5) check 0 <= qy < p, (6) verify (qx, qy) is on the secp256r1 curve, (7) verify (qx, qy) is not the point at infinity. All clients MUST implement identical ordering to ensure deterministic behavior.

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft specific 160-byte inputs targeting each validation step boundary. Different ordering between clients would manifest with edge-case inputs.

properties.severity_justification: Different validation ordering across clients leads to consensus split where one client returns success and another returns failure for the same input.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires identifying an input that produces different results across two or more client implementations due to validation order divergence.

properties.text: The p256verify signature verification MUST check that the recovered point R' is not the point at infinity before comparing r' with r. Omitting this check (as in RIP-7212) leads to implementation-dependent non-deterministic behavior.

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft inputs where the scalar multiplication results in the point at infinity by selecting specific (h, r, s, qx, qy) values.

properties.severity_justification: Missing infinity check is a known vulnerability from RIP-7212 that leads to cross-client consensus failures. A crafted signature could verify on some clients and fail on others.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Known vulnerability pattern; PoC must show a specific client missing this check.

properties.text: The p256verify signature comparison MUST use modular reduction: r' == r mod n, NOT direct equality r' == r. Direct comparison fails for edge-case x-coordinates where the elliptic curve point's x-coordinate exceeds the subgroup order n.

reachability.notes: The secp256r1 curve has n < p, so there exist valid curve points with x > n. An attacker can construct signatures where this edge case is triggered.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect comparison leads to consensus divergence. For secp256r1, the probability of n < x < p is approximately (p-n)/p, which is non-negligible for crafted inputs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC with a valid signature whose verification point x-coordinate falls in the range [n, p).

properties.text: The fixed gas cost of 6900 for p256verify MUST be sufficient to cover worst-case computational complexity across all client implementations. The precompile MUST NOT be usable as a denial-of-service vector where the actual computation time exceeds what 6900 gas represents.

reachability.notes: Attacker can submit many transactions each invoking p256verify repeatedly within the gas limit to amplify resource consumption.

properties.severity_justification: Underpriced gas could allow resource exhaustion attacks against validators, potentially causing block processing delays or missed slots.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires benchmarking showing that worst-case p256verify execution time exceeds the gas-proportionate allocation relative to other opcodes.

properties.text: The fork trigger MUST fire exactly once at FULU_FORK_EPOCH and only at an epoch boundary (slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0). Once triggered, the fork MUST be irreversible.

reachability.notes: Fork trigger executes automatically at epoch boundaries during state transition. Incorrect implementation causes chain split.

properties.severity_justification: A fork trigger bug (firing at wrong epoch, firing multiple times, or being reversible) would cause a network-wide consensus failure affecting all validators.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating that a specific client implementation handles the fork trigger incorrectly.

properties.text: The upgrade_to_fulu function MUST be pure: all fields from the pre-state (electra.BeaconState) MUST be preserved in the post-state except fork and proposer_lookahead. fork.previous_version MUST equal pre.fork.current_version. fork.current_version MUST equal FULU_FORK_VERSION. fork.epoch MUST equal get_current_epoch(pre). No side effects on pre-state may occur.

reachability.notes: Executes during the Fulu fork transition. Any field corruption would cause consensus divergence.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect state field copying during fork upgrade would corrupt the beacon state, potentially causing permanent chain split or loss of validator data.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a field that is incorrectly copied or mutated during upgrade_to_fulu in a specific client.

properties.text: compute_fork_version MUST return exactly one valid Version for any epoch value. Fork epoch constants MUST be strictly ordered: GENESIS < ALTAIR < BELLATRIX < CAPELLA < DENEB < ELECTRA < FULU.

reachability.notes: Fork version computation is used in gossip topic routing, ENR encoding, and state transitions. Wrong version causes network partition.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect fork version causes nodes to subscribe to wrong gossip topics and reject valid peers, effectively partitioning the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client with misconfigured fork epoch ordering or branching error.

properties.text: verify_data_column_sidecar MUST reject sidecars where: (1) sidecar.index >= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS, (2) kzg_commitments is empty, (3) kzg_commitments count exceeds max_blobs_per_block for the epoch, or (4) column, kzg_commitments, and kzg_proofs have unequal lengths.

reachability.notes: Any network peer can send crafted data column sidecars via gossip subnets. This is step 1 of the 13-step gossip validation pipeline.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing structural validation could allow invalid sidecars to proceed to expensive cryptographic checks or be accepted, corrupting the data availability layer.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires crafted sidecar that bypasses one of the four structural checks in a specific client.

properties.text: All cells in a data column sidecar MUST share the same cell index (equal to the column index). verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch MUST receive consistent-length arrays of commitments, cell_indices, cells, and proofs.

reachability.notes: Crafted sidecars with mismatched cell indices could bypass KZG verification if the index construction is incorrect.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect cell index construction would cause KZG verification to check wrong polynomial evaluation points, potentially accepting invalid data columns and undermining data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a sidecar where cell index mismatch causes invalid data to pass KZG verification.

properties.text: The Merkle inclusion proof for kzg_commitments MUST verify against the block body_root at depth KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH (== 4). The leaf MUST be hash_tree_root(sidecar.kzg_commitments) and the index MUST be derived from get_generalized_index(BeaconBlockBody, blob_kzg_commitments).

reachability.notes: A crafted sidecar with a valid Merkle proof for a different block body field would pass inclusion verification but bind to wrong commitments.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect inclusion proof depth or generalized index would allow sidecars to bind kzg_commitments from one block to a different block's body, breaking data integrity.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating incorrect generalized index computation in a client's SSZ implementation for the Fulu BeaconBlockBody.

properties.text: compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar MUST compute subnet_id = column_index % DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT, where DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT == 128. The result MUST always be in range [0, 128).

reachability.notes: Subnet routing is used by all nodes. Incorrect computation fragments the gossip network.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong subnet computation prevents peers from receiving data columns, degrading data availability and potentially causing missed attestations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client with incorrect subnet routing logic.

properties.text: The gossip validation pipeline for data column sidecars MUST execute exactly one path from q_init to q_final per sidecar. All REJECT checks MUST fail before a message is forwarded. IGNORE conditions MUST allow re-processing later via queuing. The deduplication key MUST be (slot, proposer_index, sidecar.index).

reachability.notes: Any peer can send sidecars triggering the validation pipeline. A bug allowing multiple paths or skipped checks enables invalid message acceptance.

properties.severity_justification: A bypass in the gossip validation pipeline could allow invalid sidecars to be accepted and forwarded, propagating corrupted data availability across the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a code path that allows an invalid sidecar to reach ACCEPT without passing all 13 validation steps.

properties.text: Proposer verification in gossip validation MUST be deferred (IGNORE instead of REJECT) if the shuffling computation is not yet available. This prevents premature rejection of valid sidecars during sync.

reachability.notes: A node syncing from behind may not have the shuffling data. Using REJECT instead of IGNORE would cause peers to penalize this node or lose valid sidecars.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect REJECT (instead of IGNORE) for proposer verification would cause valid sidecars to be permanently dropped during sync, degrading data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client that REJECTs instead of IGNOREs when proposer shuffling is unavailable.

properties.text: beacon_block_kzg_validation MUST enforce len(blob_kzg_commitments) <= get_blob_parameters(epoch).max_blobs_per_block, where max_blobs_per_block is epoch-dependent. Blocks with zero commitments MUST be valid.

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer can include maximum blob commitments. The epoch-dependent limit via BLOB_SCHEDULE adds complexity.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting a block with more blobs than allowed could cause nodes with correct limits to reject it, splitting the network at epoch boundaries where blob parameters change.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating incorrect blob parameter lookup at an epoch boundary in a specific client.

properties.text: DataColumnSidecarsByRange responses MUST contain no more than MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS sidecars. Sidecars MUST be sent in (slot, column_index) order. All sidecars of a block MUST be included if any are included. Sidecars MUST be from the current fork choice chain. The serve range MUST be [max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, FULU_FORK_EPOCH), current_epoch].

reachability.notes: Any peer can issue DataColumnSidecarsByRange requests with crafted parameters attempting to exceed response limits or access out-of-range data.

properties.severity_justification: Exceeding MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS allows resource exhaustion. Incorrect serve range computation could serve stale or invalid data.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a request that causes a client to respond with more sidecars than MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS.

properties.text: DataColumnSidecarsByRoot MUST reject requests where the total requested_columns_count (sum of columns across all identifiers) exceeds MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS. Sidecars MUST only be served for blocks passing gossip validation and not failing the beacon-chain state transition.

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft multiple DataColumnsByRootIdentifier entries with many column indices to attempt resource exhaustion.

properties.severity_justification: Missing aggregate count check allows an attacker to request far more sidecars than intended by distributing across many identifiers, causing memory/bandwidth exhaustion.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a request pattern that bypasses the aggregate limit in a specific client.

properties.text: During distributed blob publishing, blobs retrieved from the local execution layer via engine_getBlobsV2 MUST skip cryptographic verification. Publishing MUST only occur on subnets the node is subscribed to (custody or sampling). The anti-equivocation cache MUST be updated regardless of whether publishing occurs.

reachability.notes: A compromised execution layer could inject invalid blob data that bypasses verification due to the trust assumption. The anti-equivocation cache invariant prevents equivocating proposers.

properties.severity_justification: If the local EL is compromised, invalid data columns are published to the network without verification, poisoning the data availability layer. Anti-equivocation cache bypass allows conflicting sidecars.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating that a compromised EL can inject invalid blob data or that the anti-equivocation cache can be bypassed.

properties.text: BlobSidecarsByRange (deprecated) MUST be fully deprecated after FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. During the transition period, only pre-Fulu blobs MUST be served. Peers MUST NOT be penalized for requesting blob sidecars from FULU_FORK_EPOCH.

reachability.notes: During the Fulu transition, peers may legitimately request deprecated endpoints. Penalizing them would cause network fragmentation.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect deprecation handling could cause peers to be disconnected during the transition period, temporarily degrading network connectivity.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client that penalizes peers for transition-boundary requests.

properties.text: ENR eth2 field MUST always be 16 bytes (SSZ-encoded ENRForkID). For BPO forks, next_fork_version MUST remain current_fork_version while next_fork_epoch is set to the planned epoch. When no fork is planned, next_fork_version = current_fork_version and next_fork_epoch = FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH.

reachability.notes: Incorrect ENR encoding during BPO fork transitions causes peering failures with compatible nodes and potential connections to incompatible ones.

properties.severity_justification: BPO fork mishandling in ENR causes node isolation during blob parameter-only transitions, which are a new fork type in Fulu.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating incorrect ENR encoding for BPO fork scenarios in a specific client.

properties.text: The transaction gas cap GAS_CAP = 16777216 (2^24) MUST be enforced at both the transaction pool admission layer and the block validation layer. A transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 MUST be rejected at the txpool. A block containing any transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 MUST be rejected during block validation.

reachability.notes: Attacker can submit transactions with gasLimit exceeding the cap via RPC or P2P gossip. Private transaction channels (Flashbots) can bypass the txpool layer.

properties.severity_justification: A transaction with gasLimit > 2^24 that passes validation could enable worst-case computational attacks within a single transaction, as the gas cap is the primary defense against single-transaction resource exhaustion.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a bypass of the gas cap check at either the txpool or block validation layer.

properties.text: The gas cap value 16777216 MUST be identical at both the txpool validation layer and the block validation layer. Block validation MUST iterate over ALL transactions in the block. A single violating transaction MUST invalidate the entire block.

reachability.notes: If the cap values diverge between layers, transactions could pass one check but fail another, causing blocks to be built but rejected.

properties.severity_justification: Divergent gas cap values between validation layers could cause valid blocks to be rejected or invalid blocks to be accepted, leading to consensus issues.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing different gas cap constants at the txpool vs block validation layers in a client.

properties.text: The gas cap MUST apply uniformly to all transaction types (legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-4844 blob transactions, etc.) regardless of the block gas limit set by validators.

reachability.notes: A client might implement the gas cap only for certain transaction types (e.g., legacy but not EIP-4844), leaving a bypass for other types.

properties.severity_justification: A transaction type-specific bypass would allow resource exhaustion attacks through the unchecked transaction type.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a specific transaction type that bypasses the gas cap check in a client.

properties.text: The ModExp gas cost formula (EIP-7883) MUST be deterministic: for identical inputs (base_length, modulus_length, exponent_length, exponent data), all client implementations MUST compute the identical gas cost. The formula MUST be max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)) with no division by 3.

reachability.notes: Any smart contract can invoke ModExp with arbitrary inputs. Non-deterministic gas computation causes consensus split.

properties.severity_justification: Gas computation divergence between clients causes blocks to be valid on some nodes and invalid on others, splitting the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires identifying specific ModExp inputs where two clients compute different gas costs.

properties.text: The multiplication_complexity function MUST have a minimum output of 16 for all inputs. For inputs with max(base_length, modulus_length) <= 32, multiplication_complexity MUST be exactly 16.

reachability.notes: Attacker can invoke ModExp with small operands (base_length, modulus_length <= 32) to verify the minimum complexity floor.

properties.severity_justification: A complexity below 16 for small operands would underprice the precompile, enabling resource exhaustion attacks with many cheap ModExp calls.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a client that computes multiplication_complexity < 16 for small inputs.

properties.text: The iteration_count for ModExp MUST always be >= 1 for all non-trivial inputs. The max(iteration_count, 1) clamp for large exponents MUST ensure no zero-cost execution paths exist. The large exponent multiplier MUST be 16 (doubled from EIP-2565's value of 8).

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft large exponents to test the iteration count logic and multiplier value.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect multiplier (8 instead of 16) would underprice large-exponent operations by 2x, the primary vulnerability EIP-7883 is designed to fix.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client using the old multiplier (8) instead of the new one (16) post-Fusaka activation.

properties.text: The minimum gas floor for ModExp MUST be 500 (raised from 200 in EIP-2565). The gas formula MUST NOT include a division by 3. The formula is: gas = max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)).

reachability.notes: Attacker can invoke ModExp with trivial inputs to verify the 500 gas floor and with moderate inputs to check the /3 divisor is removed.

properties.severity_justification: Retaining the /3 divisor would keep gas costs 3x lower than intended, maintaining the underpricing vulnerability that becomes critical with increased block gas limits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client that still divides by 3 or uses a gas floor of 200 post-Fusaka.

properties.text: ModExp gas computation MUST NOT have integer overflow vulnerabilities. For very large max_length values, 2 * words^2 and complexity * iterations MUST be computed using sufficiently large integer types (256-bit or arbitrary precision).

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft ModExp inputs with very large length parameters. If overflow occurs, the gas could wrap to a small value.

properties.severity_justification: Integer overflow in gas computation could reduce the charged gas to near-zero for expensive operations, enabling catastrophic resource exhaustion.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a specific (base_length, modulus_length, exponent_length) tuple that triggers overflow in a client's gas computation.

properties.text: The BLOB_SCHEDULE entries MUST have unique, monotonically ordered epoch values, all >= FULU_FORK_EPOCH. All execution clients MUST implement identical BLOB_SCHEDULE configurations. Divergent schedules between clients would cause consensus failures at epoch boundaries.

reachability.notes: BLOB_SCHEDULE is a configuration-level trust anchor. Misconfiguration at epoch boundaries causes immediate consensus split.

properties.severity_justification: Divergent BLOB_SCHEDULE between clients causes validators to disagree on maximum blob counts, splitting the network at the epoch boundary.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires identifying a client with incorrect BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration values.

properties.text: The proposer_lookahead MUST shift correctly at epoch boundaries, maintaining exactly (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries. The proposer_lookahead MUST be freshly initialized via initialize_proposer_lookahead(pre) during the Fulu fork upgrade.

reachability.notes: Off-by-one errors in lookahead shift would assign wrong proposers. All validators must compute identical assignments.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect proposer assignment due to lookahead shift error causes validators to reject valid blocks or accept blocks from unauthorized proposers, splitting the chain.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating an off-by-one error in proposer_lookahead shift at an epoch boundary.

properties.text: The fork digest for gossip topics MUST incorporate blob parameters via XOR with hash(epoch + max_blobs_per_block). Different blob configurations MUST produce different fork digests, automatically segregating peers with incompatible parameters.

reachability.notes: Without blob parameter incorporation in fork digest, nodes with different blob limits could process each other's messages, causing confusion.

properties.severity_justification: Missing blob parameter incorporation in fork digest allows cross-configuration message injection, potentially causing validators to process incompatible blocks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client that does not include blob parameters in fork digest computation.

properties.text: The gossip validation pipeline for data column sidecars MUST verify the proposer BLS signature before accepting or forwarding the sidecar. Invalid signatures MUST result in REJECT. The proposer_index MUST match the expected proposer for the slot derived from beacon state shuffling.

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could forge a data column sidecar with a fabricated signed_block_header. BLS signature verification is the primary authentication gate.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing proposer signature verification would allow arbitrary data injection into the data availability layer by any network participant.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a code path where a sidecar is accepted without BLS signature verification.

properties.text: Data column sidecar integrity MUST be verified through three layers: (1) structural validation (SG-002), (2) KZG proof verification via verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (SG-003), and (3) Merkle inclusion proof verification linking kzg_commitments to the block body_root (SG-004). All three MUST pass before acceptance.

reachability.notes: A peer could tamper with cells, KZG commitments, or proofs within a sidecar. All three verification layers must be checked.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing any of the three integrity layers could inject invalid data into the data availability layer, undermining PeerDAS security guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a sidecar that passes one or two layers but contains invalid data, and is accepted by a client.

properties.text: The anti-equivocation cache MUST track sidecars by the tuple (slot, proposer_index, sidecar.index). Only the first valid sidecar for each tuple MUST be accepted; subsequent duplicates MUST be IGNORED.

reachability.notes: An equivocating proposer could publish conflicting sidecars for the same (slot, index) to different subnets.

properties.severity_justification: Anti-equivocation cache bypass would allow conflicting data columns to coexist, causing different nodes to have inconsistent views of data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a cache bypass allowing two conflicting sidecars for the same tuple to be accepted.

properties.text: The gossip validation pipeline MUST order checks from cheapest to most expensive: structural checks first, then subnet validation, then slot timing, then proposer signature, then parent/fork choice, then Merkle proof, then KZG proof, then deduplication, then proposer schedule. This ordering MUST minimize computational waste from invalid messages.

reachability.notes: An attacker flooding invalid sidecars benefits from reordered validation that places expensive checks first.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect validation ordering increases the computational cost of processing invalid messages, amplifying DoS attacks but not causing consensus failures.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating that a client performs expensive checks (KZG, BLS) before cheaper structural checks.

properties.text: For all IGNORE conditions in gossip validation (future slot, pre-finalized slot, parent not seen, duplicate sidecar, proposer shuffling unavailable), the node MUST NOT penalize the sending peer. IGNORE MUST allow re-processing later via queuing.

reachability.notes: Incorrect REJECT instead of IGNORE leaks local node state and causes valid messages to be permanently dropped.

properties.severity_justification: Using REJECT instead of IGNORE for state-dependent conditions could cause valid sidecars to be dropped and peers to be penalized, degrading network health.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client using REJECT where IGNORE is specified for a state-dependent condition.

properties.text: Block validation MUST reject a block submitted via a private transaction channel (e.g., Flashbots, MEV Boost relay) that contains any transaction with gasLimit > 16777216, even if the transaction bypassed the public txpool.

reachability.notes: Transactions submitted via Flashbots or direct-to-builder channels bypass txpool validation. Block validation is the last defense.

properties.severity_justification: If block validation can be bypassed for private-channel transactions, the entire gas cap defense-in-depth is defeated.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a block with a gas-cap-violating transaction accepted by a client via the MEV-Boost pathway.

properties.text: The KZG trusted setup parameters (KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL) MUST be loaded from a verified source and validated against known checksums. G1 and G2 elements MUST correspond to the same trusted setup ceremony.

reachability.notes: Trusted setup compromise is a supply chain attack. Runtime verification is limited. The security assumption is that the ceremony was honestly conducted.

properties.severity_justification: Compromised trusted setup allows forging valid KZG proofs for arbitrary data, completely undermining data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Trusted setup integrity is a foundational assumption, not a runtime-verifiable property.

properties.text: The Fiat-Shamir challenge for batch KZG verification MUST include ALL verifier-relevant data in the hash input: commitments, cell indices, cell evaluations, and proofs. The hash input order MUST be deterministic and canonical. The domain separator RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN MUST be unique.

reachability.notes: If the Fiat-Shamir challenge does not bind to all inputs, an adversary could substitute proofs or cells that pass batch verification.

properties.severity_justification: Incomplete Fiat-Shamir binding would allow forging batch proofs that appear valid, completely undermining data availability verification.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating that a client omits a required field from the Fiat-Shamir hash input.

properties.text: Data recovery via Reed-Solomon erasure coding MUST require at least 50% of cells (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2). Cell indices provided for recovery MUST be unique, sorted, and within valid bounds [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). Recovered polynomial MUST be truncated to degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB.

reachability.notes: A malicious requester could provide fewer than 50% cells, duplicate indices, or unsorted indices to trigger incorrect recovery.

properties.severity_justification: Recovery with insufficient or inconsistent cells produces an incorrect polynomial, which when used to regenerate proofs would create invalid sidecars.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating recovery with < 50% cells or duplicate indices producing incorrect output in a client.

properties.text: The deposit contract address MUST be exactly DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS (0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa). The deposit event signature hash MUST be exactly DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH (0x649bbc62d0e31342afea4e5cd82d4049e7e1ee912fc0889aa790803be39038c5). Only logs matching BOTH the address AND the signature hash MUST be processed as deposit events.

reachability.notes: A malicious contract at a different address could emit DepositEvent-shaped logs. Without address verification, fraudulent deposits could be injected.

properties.severity_justification: Processing deposits from a non-canonical address would inject fraudulent validator deposits into the consensus layer, potentially allowing unauthorized staking.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client that processes deposit logs from addresses other than DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS.

properties.text: extract_deposit_data MUST validate deposit event data has exactly 576 bytes total with fixed offsets: PUBKEY_OFFSET=160, WC_OFFSET=256, AMOUNT_OFFSET=320, SIGNATURE_OFFSET=384, INDEX_OFFSET=512. Any deviation MUST result in InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: A compromised deposit contract could emit malformed event data. Strict offset validation prevents misinterpreting fields.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect offset parsing would extract wrong public keys, withdrawal credentials, or amounts, corrupting the validator registry.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client that accepts deposit event data with incorrect offsets or total length.

properties.text: Receipt processing order (block_output.receipt_keys) MUST deterministically define deposit request ordering. All compliant execution clients MUST produce identical deposit_requests bytes for the same block. compute_requests_hash MUST use SHA-256 with order-preserving double-hashing.

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic deposit ordering would cause different clients to compute different requests_hash values, causing consensus split.

properties.severity_justification: Divergent deposit ordering between clients causes requests_hash mismatch, leading to network-wide consensus failure.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating two clients producing different deposit ordering for the same block.

properties.text: EIP-7702 Authorization tuple verification MUST validate: (1) chain_id matches the current chain for replay protection, (2) nonce matches the authorizer's current nonce for freshness, and (3) ECDSA signature (y_parity, r, s) recovers to the expected authorizer address.

reachability.notes: An attacker could forge or replay Authorization tuples to delegate code execution to a malicious address, taking control of the victim's account.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing Authorization verification allows unauthorized code delegation, enabling an attacker to execute arbitrary code in the context of the victim's account and steal funds.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating an Authorization replay or forgery that is accepted by a specific client.

properties.text: encode_account MUST produce deterministic, canonical RLP encoding with tuple ordering (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash). The storage_root parameter MUST be a valid 32-byte Merkle root. EMPTY_ACCOUNT MUST be an immutable frozen constant.

reachability.notes: Account encoding is an internal operation. Non-determinism would cause state root divergence but is not directly externally triggerable.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic RLP encoding would cause state root divergence between clients, leading to a permanent consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Internal encoding correctness; not directly exploitable via external entry points.

properties.text: The pairing check e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl MUST be sound: it MUST reject with overwhelming probability when the underlying KZG polynomial commitment relationship does not hold. The batch verification MUST use a single pairing check for all cells.

reachability.notes: An adversary submitting crafted cells/proofs relies on the pairing check to detect tampering. A soundness failure would accept invalid proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Pairing check unsoundness would allow forged data availability proofs, completely defeating the data availability sampling scheme.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating invalid cells/proofs that pass the pairing check in a specific client implementation.

properties.text: bytes_to_bls_field MUST validate that input bytes represent a value strictly less than BLS_MODULUS. bls_field_to_bytes and bytes_to_bls_field MUST be correct inverse operations for all valid field elements. The fixed segment size MUST be BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT.

reachability.notes: An adversary submitting blobs with byte sequences >= BLS_MODULUS could produce invalid field elements that corrupt polynomial operations.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting bytes >= BLS_MODULUS as field elements causes undefined behavior in all downstream polynomial operations, potentially producing invalid proofs that pass verification or valid proofs that fail.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a blob containing bytes >= BLS_MODULUS that are not rejected by a client's deserializer.

properties.text: Validators MUST retain data column sidecars for MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs and MUST serve them on request during this retention period. Premature pruning MUST NOT occur.

reachability.notes: Peers may request sidecars during the retention period. Premature pruning degrades data availability for the network.

properties.severity_justification: Premature sidecar pruning reduces data availability redundancy but does not directly cause consensus failures.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a client that prunes sidecars before the retention period expires.

properties.text: The custody requirement for validators MUST be proportional to stake: total_node_balance // BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP, clamped to [VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT, NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS]. The minimum VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT MUST be at least 8.

reachability.notes: Incorrect custody computation from stale beacon state could create data availability coverage gaps.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect custody assignment could leave some data columns without sufficient validator coverage, degrading data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating incorrect custody group computation in a specific client.

properties.text: The epoch processing pipeline (15 sequential sub-processes) MUST execute in strict order. State mutations from earlier steps MUST be visible to later steps. Reordering MUST produce incorrect state transitions.

reachability.notes: Epoch processing occurs automatically at each epoch boundary. Reordering sub-processes causes deterministic state divergence.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect epoch processing order causes state root divergence, leading to permanent consensus split at the next epoch boundary.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating reordered epoch sub-processes in a specific client implementation.

properties.text: The recursive FFT implementation MUST require len(vals) to be a power of 2. len(vals) MUST equal len(roots_of_unity). All protocol-defined constants (FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL) MUST be powers of 2.

reachability.notes: Non-power-of-2 input length to FFT causes incorrect recursive splits, potentially leading to infinite recursion or silent corruption.

properties.severity_justification: FFT with incorrect input length could cause client crashes (infinite recursion) or produce silently incorrect polynomial representations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating an input path that reaches FFT with non-power-of-2 length in a client.

properties.text: polynomial_eval_to_coeff MUST apply bit-reversal permutation before inverse FFT. bit_reversal_permutation MUST be applied consistently across polynomial_eval_to_coeff, coset_shift_for_cell, coset_for_cell, and recover_polynomialcoeff. Any inconsistency MUST be detectable via cross-function verification.

reachability.notes: Inconsistent bit-reversal between encoding and decoding paths produces misaligned evaluations that cause KZG proofs to fail.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent bit-reversal permutation silently produces incorrect polynomial representations, causing all generated KZG proofs to fail verification.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating inconsistent bit-reversal application in a client's polynomial operations.

properties.text: Sidecar publishing during distributed blob publishing MUST only occur on subnets the node is subscribed to via custody or sampling duties. Non-subscribed subnets MUST skip the publish step and proceed directly to cache update. The gossip layer MUST reject messages from peers not subscribed to the topic.

reachability.notes: A node publishing to non-subscribed subnets acts as an unauthorized publisher, potentially influencing data availability beyond its designated role.

properties.severity_justification: Unauthorized subnet publishing could influence data availability distribution but would be detected by receiving peers' gossip validation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a client that publishes sidecars to subnets it is not subscribed to.

properties.text: divide_polynomialcoeff MUST assert the divisor polynomial is not the zero polynomial. The leading coefficient of the divisor MUST be nonzero. Division by zero MUST cause a runtime error rather than silent corruption.

reachability.notes: During data recovery, the vanishing polynomial used as divisor could theoretically evaluate to zero if the coset domain is incorrectly chosen.

properties.severity_justification: Division by zero in polynomial operations during recovery could crash the client or produce silently incorrect recovery results.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating an input that triggers zero-divisor in polynomial division during recovery.

properties.text: interpolate_polynomialcoeff MUST require all x-values to be distinct. Duplicate x-values MUST cause a detectable error (division by zero in the field) rather than silent incorrect interpolation.

reachability.notes: An adversary providing duplicate cell indices for recovery would cause duplicate x-values in interpolation.

properties.severity_justification: Silent incorrect interpolation with duplicate points would produce a wrong polynomial, leading to invalid recovery results that may pass some checks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating duplicate cell indices reaching interpolation in a client.

properties.text: The coset FFT evaluation domain (using PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY as shift_factor) MUST avoid evaluation points where the vanishing polynomial is zero. PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY MUST be a genuine primitive root of the correct order for the BLS12-381 scalar field.

reachability.notes: Coset domain correctness is a static algebraic property of the configuration constants. Incorrect primitive root would affect all operations.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect primitive root makes all FFT and coset evaluations algebraically meaningless, breaking the entire KZG commitment scheme.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Static configuration issue; not directly exploitable by external attacker.

properties.text: After recovering a polynomial from partial cells, the high-degree coefficients (beyond FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB) MUST be verified to be zero. The recovered polynomial MUST be verified against the original KZG commitment using verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch before being used.

reachability.notes: An adversary providing inconsistent cells for recovery could produce a higher-degree polynomial that regenerates incorrect cells/proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Missing post-recovery verification allows adversarial cells to produce incorrect recovery, publishing invalid data columns to the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating that a client skips post-recovery KZG verification or degree check.

properties.text: If trie_get returns None for a key in receipt_keys, the execution client MUST halt with an assertion failure rather than silently skipping the deposit. This fail-stop behavior MUST prevent silent data loss.

reachability.notes: A malformed block could reference receipt keys that do not exist in the receipts trie, triggering the assertion.

properties.severity_justification: A crafted block that triggers assertion failure would crash the execution client. While this prevents silent data loss, it creates a DoS vector.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a block that causes trie_get to return None for a receipt key, crashing the client.

properties.text: During the Fulu transition period, deprecated BlobSidecarsByRoot MUST serve only pre-Fulu blobs. The serve range MUST be [min(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS, FULU_FORK_EPOCH), FULU_FORK_EPOCH). Peers requesting from FULU_FORK_EPOCH MUST NOT be penalized.

reachability.notes: During transition, legitimate peers may request deprecated endpoints. Serving Fulu-epoch blobs via the old protocol would be incorrect.

properties.severity_justification: Serving post-Fulu blobs via deprecated API or penalizing transition-boundary requests would cause protocol degradation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires showing a client serving post-Fulu data via deprecated BlobSidecarsByRoot or penalizing peers at the boundary.

properties.text: The constant-time execution of p256verify is NOT guaranteed by EIP-7951. Implementations MAY leak timing information about private keys to co-located observers. This is a known, accepted trade-off in the specification.

reachability.notes: Timing side-channel requires co-located attacker (same physical machine). The specification explicitly does not mandate constant-time execution.

properties.severity_justification: Requires physical co-location with the target validator. The specification explicitly acknowledges this trade-off, favoring performance over side-channel resistance.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Explicitly out-of-scope per the EIP-7951 specification. Known and accepted design trade-off.
